title: Whittled hazel cheese spreader
subtitle: A simple palette knife shape from a hazel stick
excerpt: A hazel cheese spreader: 18 cm long, with a flat paddle blade 6 cm by 2.5 cm and a round handle 10 cm long. Whittled from a single hazel stick with a sloyd knife and a detail knife. A quick project that needs no special tools beyond a sharp knife and a strop.
sourceNotes: Traditional British woodland craft; simple spreading tools in green hazel documented in W. P. Westell, Woodland Crafts of Britain (1910).

glossaryTerms.definition: Freshly cut or recently felled wood, still high in moisture content. Hazel cuts easily with a sharp knife while green; it hardens as it dries.
A carving stroke where the knife is pushed forward away from the body. Good for long shaping cuts on straight grain.
A shallow cut made perpendicular to the grain to define a boundary. Prevents a following paring cut from splitting past the intended line.

content.text: : 18 cm long, with a thin flat blade and a round handle. The whole shape is cut from one straight hazel stick about 20 mm in diameter. It needs only a sloyd knife and a detail knife. The project takes about forty minutes start to finish. Hazel hardens as it dries; a spreader carved in green hazel is stiff and durable within a week.
Knife direction: cut away from the body at all times. Never draw the knife toward the thumb of the hand holding the work.
Sharp edge: a sharp knife is safer than a dull one. Strop before and during each session.
First aid: styptic pencil, gauze, and dressing within reach. Firm pressure on a cut, elevate. A cut that shows fat or will not close goes to A&E.

A straight hazel stick, 20 to 22 mm in diameter, 22 cm long. Hazel from coppice or hedge management is usually available from woodland groups or countryside volunteers. The stick should have no side branches and a consistent diameter. If hazel is not available, a similar-diameter straight-grained ash, birch, or sycamore branch works identically.

Mark two zones on the stick: the handle (10 cm from the base end) and the blade area (6 cm from the tip, with a 2 cm shoulder zone between handle and blade). The shoulder zone becomes the narrowing where blade meets handle. Draw the blade outline on the flat face with a pencil: the blade is 6 cm long and 25 mm wide, centred on the stick width.

Then taper the blade edges: take thin slices from each long edge at about 30 degrees until the edge is 1 mm thick. A cheese spreader does not need a sharp edge; 1 mm is enough.

Then peel back from the handle side to meet the stop cut, narrowing the shoulder to about 12 mm. This forms the waist between blade and handle. Work the shoulder with the detail knife for cleaner control in the tight area.

The handle keeps most of its original round form; just clean up the bark and any rough spots with light push cuts. Round the base end with the sloyd knife. The bark can be left on or peeled off; hazel bark is smooth and pleasant to hold, and leaving it gives a natural look.

Leave the spreader to dry for one week before use. No finish is necessary; hazel is food-safe and naturally hard. A light wipe of walnut oil after drying conditions the surface and darkens the wood slightly. Re-oil two or three times a year if the wood looks dry.

attrs.symptom: The blade is uneven in thickness
attrs.cause: Strokes were not keeping the flat face parallel as material was removed.
attrs.fix: Hold the blade up to the light and look along the face to find the high spots. Take light strokes on the high spots only, checking between each pass.

attrs.symptom: The wood is splitting at the shoulder rather than cutting cleanly
attrs.cause: The paring cut reached the shoulder before the stop cut was deep enough.
attrs.fix: Stop cutting. Re-deepen the stop cut, going to 5 mm. Then approach from the handle side again with a lighter stroke.

attrs.cause: The blade was made too thin (under 3 mm) in green hazel, which shrinks across the grain as it dries.
attrs.fix: Keep the blade at least 4 mm thick at the centre. The edges can taper to 1 mm, but the middle section needs structural thickness.
